explanation: The act where a person betrays or hands over someone they trust, as Judas Iscariot did to Jesus by selling him for silver coins.
Twenty silver coins that were the price of slavery and paid to Judas for his betrayal of Jesus.
A religious practice where one abstains from food or drink for a period, often used together with prayer before important events.
The food that was central during the Passover feast and symbolizes the innocent sacrifice offered for sins.
The cross-shaped stake or structure on which Jesus would later be executed, a symbol of suffering and sacrifice.
An olive garden outside Jerusalem where Jesus entered deep sorrow and prayer before his arrest.
The physical reaction in Jesus as he sweated blood during his intense spiritual struggle and pain in the garden.
Arrest or detention of a person by authorities, which happened to Jesus when he was taken into custody by the temple guards.
The act where the disciples abandoned Jesus and fled after his arrest, while Peter later denied him three times.
Title for the supreme religious leader in Judaism under Roman rule, which Caiaphas held when he presided over the trial of Jesus.
The act where a person renounces their faith or allegiance, as Peter did by saying three times that he did not know Jesus.
The High Priest's council (Sanhedrin) which gathered to judge Jesus and find him guilty of blasphemy.
The fluid from the body that symbolizes life, sacrifice, and forgiveness of sins, central to the Last Supper where Jesus shared wine with his disciples.
